principle: Actual asked clauses only; scenario givens and source-backed contextual background are not extra response requirements. No reader/grade/performance history in this source-review packet.

entries.asked_question: How are starting properties and money assigned, where do the dealt cards go, and how is the End of Game card inserted?
required_answer_facts: Remove End of Game, shuffle, deal two property cards per player.
Mark the two initial lots and take starting money equal to the sum of their printed card money values.
Discard by color/Strip with counts visible.
Divide remaining shuffled deck into four roughly equal stacks; End of Game on top of fourth, other three on top.
contextual_key_background: These card values are only used during setup; Q03 asks that limitation explicitly.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up; unified p5

entries.asked_question: Who takes the first turn, how does turn order proceed, and what is the normal Draw/Play sequence?
required_answer_facts: Each rolls two dice; highest roller takes player card and first turn.
Pass player card left after each turn.
Draw property card, take its lot, pay all owned lots, pay/score indicated casinos, discard appropriately, then Play actions.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Taking Turns/On Every Turn; p3 Ending Step 1

entries.asked_question: You draw the card for an empty lot. When is it acquired and paid, and do the printed card starting-money values pay again?
required_answer_facts: Place your marker before payouts.
The newly acquired marked lot pays you $1 in the coming lot payout.
Card money values are used only during setup, not drawn-turn income.
contextual_key_background: All other marked lots also pay their owners $1, tested by Q02/Q06.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up/Take Over Your Lot/Owned Lots Pay

entries.asked_question: You draw a lot card for a sprawled tile with an opponent’s 5, although the board prints 2. What happens to the tile and die, and who receives its imminent matching-color money?
required_answer_facts: Tile stays; replace opposing die with your own retaining current value 5, not printed 2.
Takeover precedes payout; you, the drawing player/new owner, receive the imminent matching-color money for the replaced die.
contextual_key_background: At current value5 that die yields $5, but Q04 asks who receives the money, not its amount. The die retains value5 as explicitly asked. Per-pip arithmetic is tested directly by Q06/Q24.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid

entries.asked_question: When do same-color tiles form one casino, can they be divided, and is the boss determined by total pips or something else?
required_answer_facts: Edge-connected same-color tiles on same block form a single indivisible casino; diagonal-only contact does not.
Boss is owner of highest individual die, not greatest total pips or most tiles.
contextual_key_background: Casino colors do not denote player colors.
entries.source_references: Original p1 Casino Tiles/Player Dice; p2 Who Owns What

entries.asked_question: A three-tile gold casino contains Red 5 and Blue 3 and 2; Red also owns two marked lots. On a gold payout, how much money and how many points does each receive from these holdings?
required_answer_facts: Red receives $7: $5 die plus $2 lots.
Blue receives $5 from dice.
Red boss receives 3 casino points, Blue no casino points.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Owned Lots Pay/Money Paid/Points Earned

entries.asked_question: How does Pay The Strip differ from a color payout, and what qualifies a casino whose only one tile touches The Strip?
required_answer_facts: Color pays all casinos of that color anywhere.
Strip pays all colors with at least one casino edge adjacent to Strip.
Entire qualifying casino pays money/points for all tiles, not only touching tile.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Pay Based on Color/Pay The Strip; unified p8

entries.asked_question: Which actions may you take in Play, in what order and how often, and may another player perform an action on your turn?
required_answer_facts: Build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, gamble in any order.
All may repeat except gamble once per own turn; reorganization also limited per die per turn.
No player takes actions on another player’s turn.
contextual_key_background: Trading may occur at any time subject to exceptions; tested by Q17/Q27/Q32.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Step 2 Play/Reorganize; p4 Trading

entries.asked_question: How do you build on your marked lot whose board price is $6 and printed die is 2? State cost, marker and die handling, and tile choice.
required_answer_facts: Pay $6; choose available casino tile color.
Remove/reclaim marker, place tile and your die set to printed board value2.
contextual_key_background: The question gives your marked lot. Build ownership eligibility is explicitly tested by Q37, not credited from this scenario given.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Build; unified p10 Build

entries.asked_question: You boss a gold casino and want to sprawl onto an edge-adjacent empty unowned $9 lot with printed die 3. What do you pay and place, and may you instead sprawl onto an opponent’s marked lot or a merely diagonal lot?
required_answer_facts: Pay $18, place available gold tile with own die 3.
The stated eligible lot is empty/unowned and edge-adjacent; opponent-marked and diagonal-only targets are illegal.
Cannot sprawl without available tile of same color.
contextual_key_background: The question already gives that the acting player is the casino boss; no need to restate a given as an extra fact.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Sprawl

entries.asked_question: How does remodeling a two-tile casino work, including eligibility, cost, tile supply, and a merger with a neighboring casino whose highest die beats yours?
required_answer_facts: Must boss casino; remodel all its tiles into one new color with enough available tiles.
Pay $10 ($5 each); replace all tiles with new-color tiles; dice/holdings remain.
Edge-adjacent same-color casinos merge; in the stated case, the neighboring casino’s higher-die owner becomes boss of the merged casino.
Return replaced old-color tiles to their supply.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Remodel and example; unified p11

entries.asked_question: May a non-boss with one die reorganize a casino with dice 5, 3 and 2? State who pays how much, which dice roll and who rolls them, and where multiple dice may return.
required_answer_facts: Yes, at least one own die suffices; acting player pays $10 total pips of all dice.
All dice reroll, each owner rolling their own.
Each owner returns dice only to their own original tiles, choosing assignment among those tiles if multiple.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize

entries.asked_question: A die was reorganized earlier this turn and its casino then merges into a larger casino. Can the larger casino be reorganized this turn, and are free boss-tie rerolls prohibited too?
required_answer_facts: No: no die may be reorganized more than once per turn, so any previously reorganized die prevents reorganization of the enlarged casino.
Boss-tie rerolls are free and not subject to reorganization once-per-turn limit.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize; p4 Reroll if Tied; unified p11

entries.asked_question: After a merger, Red 5 and Blue 5 tie above Green 4. What rerolls, at what cost, and who bosses if both 5s reroll to 3? What if all largest tied dice belong to one player, or only smaller dice tie?
required_answer_facts: Immediately reroll only tied largest dice at no cost.
If both become 3, Green unchanged 4 is boss; do not keep rerolling smaller 3s.
Same-player highest tie requires no reroll; ties below highest require none.
If different players remain tied for current highest, repeat with current highest until one player controls highest.
entries.source_references: Original p4 After Each Action Reroll if Tied and diagram

entries.asked_question: You have $18 and gamble at an opponent’s four-tile casino whose boss has $15. What is the maximum bet, who gets the House card, and how many times may you gamble this turn?
required_answer_facts: Maximum $15: minimum of $20 tile cap, own $18 and boss $15.
Gamble once during own turn.
Give the casino boss the House card.
contextual_key_background: Casino must be bossed by another player.
entries.source_references: Original p4 Gamble

entries.asked_question: For a legal $4 bet against a boss who has $7, resolve every possible two-dice sum group, including the limited doubled payout. Is a winning bettor also losing their stake?
required_answer_facts: 3/4/9/10/11: win $4 from boss and retain/get stake back.
2/12: nominal win $8 but receive only boss’s available $7 and retain/get stake back.
5/6/7/8: lose/pay $4 to boss.
entries.source_references: Original p4 Gamble; unified p13

entries.asked_question: What may be traded, when may trading occur, how are traded lots and dice transferred, and what cannot be promised or traded?
required_answer_facts: Trade money, lots, casino dice and actions on the active player’s current turn. Trading may occur even off-turn, except no initiated trades during unresolved boss ties or after End of Game is drawn.
Replace lot marker with recipient marker; replace die with recipient die at same current pip value, not board value.
No points or casino tiles; no promises of future-turn actions/exchanges/transfers.
No actions on another player’s turn.
entries.source_references: Original p4 Trading; unified physicalp9 Settling Who’s the Boss, physicalp15 Trading, physicalp16 Winning.

entries.asked_question: Starting at score 8, where do single casino awards of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 points leave you? Can two separate one-tile casinos combine their awards, and in what order are different casinos scored?
required_answer_facts: 1 leaves 8; 2 or 3 reaches 10; 4 or 5 reaches 12.
Insufficient excess at a break is lost; cannot pool separate casino awards.
Score each casino independently smallest to largest, player chooses equal-size order; two single-tile awards leave 8.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Scoring; p3 scoring example and multiple casinos

entries.asked_question: What happens when the End of Game card is drawn, including remaining actions, final payouts, winner and tied score? Is there an immediate alternative win condition?
required_answer_facts: Game ends immediately; no subsequent Play actions.
Final payout all owned lots and casinos touching Strip, with ordinary money and scoring rules.
Most points wins; tied most points breaks by most money.
90+ points wins immediately in base game.
entries.source_references: Original p4 Winning; unified p16

entries.asked_question: In two-player play, what happens to F cards drawn during setup and during a turn? May anyone build on F, and can a turn pay more than once before actions?
required_answer_facts: No building on F block.
Discard and replace an F card drawn during setup; use accepted A–E starting cards.
During turn do not mark F; pay owned lots and indicated casinos/points, discard then repeat Draw until A–E card resolved.
Each such draw pays, so multiple payouts occur in one turn before Play.
contextual_key_background: An End of Game draw interrupts immediately; Q19 and Q32 test end priority.
The accepted starting cards determine initial properties and money; that normal setup resource calculation is asked by Q01, not an extra Q20 requirement.
entries.source_references: Original p4 2-Player Rules/Winning; unified p16 2-Player Rules

entries.asked_question: All nine gold tiles are on the board. Can you build another gold tile using the spare tenth tile, sprawl a gold casino, or remodel a three-tile casino to gold? May you build a different available color?
required_answer_facts: The tenth is a replacement, not a tenth usable tile.
Cannot build gold, sprawl gold or remodel to gold without sufficient available tiles.
Yes, a different available color may be built on an owned lot.
contextual_key_background: Normal build cost applies; this question does not give a price or ask a monetary calculation.
entries.source_references: Original p1 Casino Tiles; p3 Available Tiles/Build/Sprawl/Remodel

entries.asked_question: All twelve of your dice are on the board when you build, sprawl or inherit a sprawled tile. How do you place the required die, what happens to the vacated tile and its scoring, and what if it was the casino’s only die?
required_answer_facts: Remove one of your existing ownership dice and place it on the new tile at the value required by the placement.
Vacated tile remains ownerless but counts for casino points.
If no dice remain in a casino it has no owner/boss.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Available Dice; unified p6 Available Dice

entries.asked_question: A property draw claims a sprawled casino tile with no die; the board prints 2, while the die removed from it used to be 5. What die do you place, does the tile change, and when does its matching casino pay?
required_answer_facts: Place own die at printed board value 2; former removed value 5 is not retained.
Casino tile remains; acquisition precedes matching casino payment.
contextual_key_background: The new value2 die pays its owner $2 on that payout, but income amount is not asked here.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid; unified p7

entries.asked_question: You draw the card for your own sprawled tile, whose die is now 6 although the board prints 2. Does ownership or value change, and what does that die earn if its casino pays?
required_answer_facts: Leave your existing die unchanged at 6.
Matching payout pays you $6 for that die.
entries.source_references: Unified p7 Step 2; original p2 Money Paid

entries.asked_question: All ten of your markers are on lots and you acquire another empty lot. How is ownership marked, what happens to the vacated lot, and which of the two lots receives the coming owned-lot payout?
required_answer_facts: Move one existing marker to newly gained lot.
You no longer own vacated lot; it does not pay you lot income.
New marked lot pays you $1 in upcoming payout.
entries.source_references: Unified p6 Available Player Markers; original p2 Draw/Owned Lots Pay

entries.asked_question: May a player conceal money or piece counts, forbid inspection of a discard pile, or deny a bank payout because the physical bank is empty?
required_answer_facts: Money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discards.
Bank money unlimited; physical bank exhaustion does not cancel a payout.
entries.source_references: Original p1 Money; unified p6 Your Resources/Available Money

entries.asked_question: A casino has two Red 6s and a Blue 3. During a trade one Red 6 is replaced by Green’s die. What value does Green’s die have, must anything reroll before further trades or actions, and who rolls?
required_answer_facts: Green’s replacement die retains value6.
The remaining Red6 and new Green6 are tied for highest across different players; reroll those two dice immediately, not Blue3 initially.
Finish resolving any current-highest cross-player ties before actions or initiating more trades; after each reroll reassess the current highest dice and stop when one player owns the highest value.

For physical roller identity, the supplied free boss-tie rules do not explicitly designate who throws each die. They specify which owners’ dice participate. The each-player-rolls-own instruction is expressly part of paid Reorganization, not a stated universal free-tie actor rule. Do not invent a mandatory owner-only allocation or an any-person permission.
contextual_key_background: Boss-tie rerolls are free; Q14 explicitly asks cost, Q27 does not.
entries.source_references: Original p4 Trading/Reroll if Tied and its narrative/example; unified physicalp9 Settling Who’s the Boss; originalp3/unifiedp11 Reorganize for the expressly local roller instruction.
entries.scope_note: Question wording is retained. Answer both which dice participate and whether the authoritative books prescribe a physical thrower. This source-limits answer does not pretend an official mandatory actor has been recovered.
entries.source_limit: No explicit mandatory physical-roller assignment appears in the supplied authority. A definite mandatory actor would require an applicable official clarification; do not infer one from Reorganization.

entries.asked_question: You draw a card and replace one of Red’s tied highest 5s in a casino with your own 5; another Red 5 remains. Is the boss tie postponed until after payment or Play, and does this reroll count as a paid reorganization?
required_answer_facts: Resolve cross-player highest tie immediately on takeover before casino payouts, not postponed to Play.
Reroll only current highest dice free; this is not paid reorganization and does not use its limit.
entries.source_references: Unified p7 Step 2/p9 Settling Who’s the Boss; p11 Reorganize

entries.asked_question: May you reorganize a casino where you alone own all dice, or one where you own none? Does reorganizing only one of your dice avoid paying for the opponents’ pips?
required_answer_facts: Sole owner may reorganize; no-own-die casino may not.
Reorganization always rerolls every die and costs all pips, including opponents, not just selected own dice.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize; unified p11

entries.asked_question: All twelve of your ownership dice are on casino tiles. Must you remove a tile’s die just to gamble, and may you gamble at your own casino if no opponent bosses any casino?
required_answer_facts: Any dice may be used to gamble; no ownership placement or removal required for the gambling roll.
Cannot gamble at own casino; if no opponent bosses a casino there is no legal gambling action.
entries.source_references: Unified p6 Available Dice; p13 Gamble

entries.asked_question: On your turn you trade for an opponent’s die so that you can reorganize their casino, then promise to pay them for a sprawl only if the reorganization gives you control. If the reroll does not make you boss so the agreed sprawl cannot happen, do the subsequent steps of the trade proceed? Could the opponent instead perform the sprawl on your turn?
required_answer_facts: When an element of trade is prevented, subsequent steps do not occur.
Opponent cannot take action on your turn.
contextual_key_background: The scenario itself gives that failed boss control means the agreed sprawl cannot happen. This is not an independently asked rule in Q31; Q36 now explicitly tests boss-only sprawl eligibility.
entries.source_references: Unified p15 Trading; original p3 Sprawl/p4 Trading
entries.scope_note: The proposed sprawl is an intended action by the active player during this same turn. Question wording is preserved. No future-turn promise or off-turn action is authorized.

entries.asked_question: The End of Game card has just been drawn. Before the final payout, may players initiate a last-minute trade of money or a casino die, perhaps to change who wins a tied score?
required_answer_facts: No: End of Game draw immediately ends play, so players cannot initiate a money/die trade before final payouts.
contextual_key_background: Final lots and Strip payouts, score/money win comparison are already asked by Q19; they are not additional requirements for this trade-priority question.
entries.source_references: Original p4 Winning; unified physical p16 Winning, first paragraph (no actions or initiated trades on End of Game draw).

entries.asked_question: During setup, which pieces does each player take, and where is each player’s scoring chip placed before the first turn?
required_answer_facts: Each player takes an action card and the scoring chip, markers and dice of one player color. Place every player’s scoring chip on 0 on the scoring track.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up, first and third paragraphs; unified physical p5 Setting Up.

entries.asked_question: Must a trade be between exactly two players, or may three players participate in one agreed trade of their money, lots and casino dice?
required_answer_facts: Any number of players may be involved in a trade, so a three-player trade is permitted, subject to the ordinary restrictions on traded assets and timing.
entries.source_references: Unified physical p15 At Any Time: Trading, first paragraph: any number of players may be involved. Original p4 Trading supplies base assets and restrictions.
entries.scope_note: A yes/no permission and any-number actor rule resolve the question. Ordinary restrictions remain valid context; do not require repeating all trading timing/assets/transfer rules.

entries.asked_question: Besides taking their own components, what banking role must the group assign during setup?
required_answer_facts: Choose a player to be the Banker.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up, second paragraph; unified physical p5 Setting Up.

entries.asked_question: You have a die in a casino, but another player is its boss. May you sprawl that casino during your own turn?
required_answer_facts: No. Only the boss may sprawl a casino; merely owning a die is insufficient.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Action–Sprawl; unified physicalp10 Sprawl.

entries.asked_question: May you use Build on an empty unowned lot or another player’s marked lot, or must the target be a lot you own?
required_answer_facts: Build may be used only on a lot you own. An unowned lot or another player’s marked lot is not a legal Build target.
entries.source_references: Original p3 Action–Build; unified physicalp10 Build.

entries.asked_question: Next to a casino you boss is an edge-adjacent, built casino tile of another color with no die. Is it a legal Sprawl target because it is unowned, or must the target be an empty lot?
required_answer_facts: No. A built casino tile remains on the board even without a die; it is a casino space, not an empty lot. Sprawl requires an empty, unowned lot, so you cannot sprawl onto or replace this tile.
entries.source_references: Original p2 Who Owns What; p3 Available Dice and Action–Sprawl; unified physicalp6 Available Dice and p10 Sprawl.
entries.scope_note: Origin boss and adjacency are givens; the asked distinction is unowned-but-occupied casino tile versus an empty lot. Different casino color is an ordinary legal scenario given preventing automatic preexisting merger, not an expansion effect.
